content.title: How many golfers have won consecutive Masters Tournaments?
content.text: It's two green jackets in as many years for Rory McIlroy. The 36-year-old from Northern Ireland defended his Masters Tournament title in the 2026 edition of the golf major, closing out the wire-to-wire win with a one-stroke edge in the final round. McIlroy had a share of the lead after round one, then pulled out to a six-shot lead after 36 holes before entering Sunday tied for the lead. In 2025, McIlroy held off Justin Rose in a playoff at Augusta National Golf Club in Georgia to win his first green jacket. The major tournament triumph made McIlroy just the sixth golfer to ever win the sport's career grand slam (winning all four majors). But just how rare is it for a golfer to win consecutive Masters? Here's what to know: Has a golfer ever won consecutive Masters Tournaments? Yes, but it's extremely rare. 0:56Rory McIlroy becomes first player to repeat at Masters since Tiger Woods Rory McIlroy won the 2026 Master tournament, becoming the first player to win back-to-back Masters since Tiger Woods in 2001-2002. How many times has a golfer won consecutive Masters Tournaments? There have been just four golfers to go back-to-back at the Masters: Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo, Tiger Woods and now McIlroy. No one has ever won three straight tournaments. Who was the last golfer to win consecutive Masters? Before McIlroy, there hadn't been a repeat Masters winner in more than two decades. Woods was the last to accomplish the feat, winning the tournament in 2001 and 2002. Here's a full look at each back-to-back Masters triumph: Jack Nicklaus: 1965-66 Nick Faldo: 1989-90 Tiger Woods: 2001-02 Rory McIlroy: 2025-26 Who gives the Masters winner the green jacket if it's a repeat winner? The Masters chairman presents the jacket to the winner if it is a repeat from the year prior. Fred Ridley is the current Masters chairman, holding the title since 2017. Who has won the most Masters? Nicklaus has the most Masters titles with six followed by Woods with five. Arnold Palmer is the only other golfer to win the tournament at least four times, while Faldo, Mickelson, Gary Player, Jimmy Demaret and Sam Snead have three titles.
